subtitle: Three-Axis Spatial Panner
tagline: Reliable stereo panning with added cues for height, distance, and front-to-back position, rendered for speakers or for headphones with KEMAR HRTF.

body.lead: TB XYZ Panner keeps dependable stereo panning at its core and adds procedural cues for height, distance, and front-to-back perspective.

body.p: The top view places a source left, right, in front, or behind without changing its distance. The side view shapes elevation and depth through level, tone, and early-reflection behaviour. Stereo mode gives solid conventional placement; Headphones mode uses KEMAR HRTF rendering for a more immersive binaural image. ROOM and OUTPUT finish the space.

ul: Top view for left/right and front/back, side view for height and distance
Three distance curves: Physical, Near Field, and Linear
STEREO rendering for speakers, HEADPHONES rendering with KEMAR HRTF
On surround outputs, the non-LFE channels are mapped by speaker direction

steps: Position (PAN, FRONT/BACK, HEIGHT, DISTANCE) and ROOM

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB XYZ Panner 1.3.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 1.0.2 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB XYZ Panner on a mono or stereo track. By default the source is centred, in front, at ear height, close, with `ROOM` at 35%.
Choose `STEREO` {{1}} for speakers or `HEADPHONES` for binaural listening.
Place the source left or right and front or back in the top view {{3}}, or with `PAN` and `FRONT/BACK` {{5}}.
Set height and distance in the side view {{4}}, or with `HEIGHT` and `DISTANCE`.
Add space with `ROOM` {{6}} and set the level with `OUTPUT` {{7}}.

ui.caption: Captured from version 1.2. Version 1.3.0 adds a DISTANCE CURVE selector (PHYSICAL, NEAR FIELD, LINEAR); the other controls are the same.

tip.text: Check a mix made in Headphones mode on speakers too, and the other way round. HRTF cues that work on headphones can sound coloured on speakers.

body.p: Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Push an element back
recipes.use: Make a pad or backing vocal sit behind the lead.
steps: Raise DISTANCE until the element sits behind the lead, then adjust ROOM for depth.

recipes.title: Overhead effect on headphones
recipes.use: A sound that seems to come from above.
steps: Keep the source in front at first; height cues are clearer from the front.

recipes.title: Behind the listener
recipes.use: Ambience or effects that come from behind on headphones.
steps: Front-back cues are subtle on speakers; check them on headphones.

recipes.title: Even, predictable fades
recipes.use: Distance automation with a simple level curve.
steps: Automate DISTANCE and listen to the level change across the move.

rows: The sound is too quiet when far away.
Distance lowers the level. Try another DISTANCE CURVE, or raise OUTPUT up to 0 dB.
Height or front-back is hard to hear on speakers.
These cues are strongest in HEADPHONES mode.
HRTF filtering changes the tone. Use STEREO for speaker mixes.
Check the track's channel layout in the host; support for surround layouts can vary by host.
Added the Physical, Near Field, and Linear distance attenuation curves, with Physical as the default.
